structured_output.hypothesis: If the claim holds, then in hollow-horned ruminants (Bovidae) the left horn's 3D centerline, after reflection through the sagittal plane, matches the right horn's centerline, so curvature is equal and torsion is equal in magnitude and opposite in sign.
structured_output.pass_criterion: In a sample of at least 30 adult spiral-horned bovid individuals with both horns scanned in 3D, the median ratio of the mirror-reflected left horn centerline's RMS deviation from the right horn centerline to the horn length is below 0.05. In addition, at least 90% of individuals show opposite-sign torsion between the two horns, and the mean absolute difference in curvature is below 10%.
structured_output.fail_criterion: The median normalized RMS deviation after mirror reflection is 0.10 or more. Alternatively, fewer than 75% of individuals show opposite-sign torsion, or the mean absolute curvature difference is 20% or more.
structured_output.interpretation: "Conjugate spirals" and "mirror image" are read as follows. After reflection through the sagittal plane, the left horn's growth centerline should superpose on the right horn's. Curvature should be equal and torsion equal in magnitude with opposite sign. The test uses 3D scans or landmark-and-semilandmark curves of both horns. It is not a test of horn length alone. Length and circumference asymmetry in the literature is fluctuating or directional asymmetry, which is a small deviation from exact symmetry. The modern reading allows small developmental noise, so the thresholds are tolerances and do not demand exact symmetry.
structured_output.no_dataset_reason: I searched for a public dataset with paired left and right bovid horn 3D geometry, meaning scans, centerlines or landmark curves. I found none that I could open and verify. The closest items were not usable. The Imperial College MRes dissertation on 3D horn variation in Bovidae is access-restricted. The Harary and Tal horn scans are supplementary material to a paper and have no dataset landing page. The cattle, goat and mouflon asymmetry studies report only horn length and circumference in article tables, with no deposited raw data. The Dryad mule deer record covers antlers, not horns. I fetched no landing page with WebFetch, so I name no dataset rather than risk an unverified identifier. A future test could use MorphoSource bovid skull scans, but I did not identify a specific verified project.

input.fail_criterion: The median normalized RMS deviation after mirror reflection is 0.10 or more. Alternatively, fewer than 75% of individuals show opposite-sign torsion, or the mean absolute curvature difference is 20% or more.
input.interpretation: "Conjugate spirals" and "mirror image" are read as follows. After reflection through the sagittal plane, the left horn's growth centerline should superpose on the right horn's. Curvature should be equal and torsion equal in magnitude with opposite sign. The test uses 3D scans or landmark-and-semilandmark curves of both horns. It is not a test of horn length alone. Length and circumference asymmetry in the literature is fluctuating or directional asymmetry, which is a small deviation from exact symmetry. The modern reading allows small developmental noise, so the thresholds are tolerances and do not demand exact symmetry.
